messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2 detected: Token accounting anomaly for tenant 'omega_enterprises' on dedicated-pool-7 (vpc-us-west-2). Sudden token_count deltas and customer 429s. Please acknowledge and triage. Link: https://redwood/incidents/1719954321

marta: acked. i'm taking lead. kevin, can you grab the edge estimator logs + recent proxy traces for that tenant?

kevin: grabbing now. quick tail of estimator log around spike (scrubbed):
```
[2024-06-30T16:22:10Z] est_req_id=zx99 tenant=omega_enterprises pool=dedicated-pool-7 fast_estimate_tokens=600 estimator_version=1.9.2 payload_bytes=1200 content_type=application/json
[2024-06-30T16:22:10Z] serve_req_id=zx99-serve runtime_token_count=6800 runtime_tokenizer=tok_v3
[2024-06-30T16:22:10Z] response_status=429 reason=tokens_over_limit
```
Note: fast_estimate only ever saw 600 tokens, runtime counted 6800. Payload bytes small-ish.

li: i pulled a sample from their upload pipeline (redacted): appears to contain NUL bytes and wide-char sequences. When i attempted to decode as utf-8 it succeeded but produced replacement chars; decoding as utf-16le produced correct text. Their client library v2.4.1 on Windows had a change that writes JSON as UTF-16LE without charset in Content-Type header.

marta: that matches a hypothesis: edge estimator assumes utf-8 and uses byte-length -> token heuristic; runtime (which runs full decode/tokenize) negotiates encoding differently or uses heuristics that detect utf-16 and decodes properly -> different token counts. Which side is over-counting? Looks like runtime tokenizes correctly for UTF-16 text producing 6800 tokens; estimator under-counted at 600. But customer sees throttles and inflated billing.

kevin: confirmed: the estimator's heuristic assumes 1 byte ~= 1 char for quick token guess and multiplies by avg_token_size=4. For UTF-16 input the bytes are 2 per char so estimator underestimates the number of multi-byte codepoints that become many BPE tokens. However we also have cases where pre-encoded base64 snippets are sent which produce opposite effects. Multiple mismatch vectors.

marta: immediate mitigation suggestions:
- Option A: For affected tenant, disable fast-edge quota checks for 1 hour so runtime's full tokenizer decides throttles (slower but accurate).
- Option B: Insert a lightweight encoding sniff at the proxy that checks for UTF-16 patterns (BOM or frequent NULs) and normalize body to UTF-8 for estimator, leaving original body for runtime.
- Option C: Temporarily raise per-tenant token limit multiplier to allow jobs to finish while we investigate billing.

li: i can deploy a proxy filter that detects BOMs and common utf-16 signatures; it takes ~2 hours to code + test small canary.

kevin: we should also check billing pipeline: any invoices generated in last 3 hours for omega_enterprises?

billing-bot: billing: invoices: none finalized for omega_enterprises in last 24h. I've placed provisional flag on account 'omega_enterprises' and opened ticket BILL-9876. Please include INCIDENT-1719954321 in billing notes.

marta: sounds good. i'm going to apply Option A for emergency: disable fast-edge quota checks for tenant. Doing admin action now: 
```
POST https://admin.internal/tenants/omega_enterprises/overrides
{ "edge_quota_mode":"disabled", "reason":"emergency - encoding mismatch causing false throttles" }
```
Response: 200 OK, override_id=ovr-20240630-01

marta: after override, replayed blocked requests in staging replay and they completed without 429. Pushing message to customer that we applied a temporary override and are pausing billing until we clear root cause.

li: deploying proxy-sniff canary to canary-host-3 in vpc-us-west-2. Will monitor. PR opened: github.com/redwood/proxy/pull/1427. Tests include UTF-16LE, UTF-16BE, BOM/no-BOM, CRLF combos.

kevin: follow-ups for postmortem: ensure estimator and runtime use same tokenizer code/version (tok_v3 vs tok_v2 mismatch seen in logs). Add integration test to run estimator vs runtime tokenization on sample payload set. Also add a telemetry metric for estimator-vs-runtime delta per-tenant to surface large divergences.

marta: onboarding note for CS: ask customers to include Content-Type charset header or to avoid sending pre-encoded binary blobs in text fields. We'll add guidance in tenant onboarding docs.

ops-runbook-bot: runbook updated with flow 'tenant-tokenizer-encoding' including steps: detect -> tenant override -> deploy proxy sniff -> escalate to billing. Link: https://runbooks.internal/tenant-tokenizer-encoding

kevin: small risk note: bypassing edge quota checks means we rely on runtime capacity; if a malicious tenant intentionally sends massive decoded text we could exhaust pool. Mitigation: set temporary per-tenant CPU/GPU rate limiter on dedicated pool to protect cluster while override is active.

marta: applied soft rate limit to their pool: 20% of pool capacity reserved, rest can process. Admin call: 
```
POST /admin/pools/dedicated-pool-7/limits
{ "tenant_reservations": [{ "tenant":"omega_enterprises","min_share":0.05,"max_share":0.2 }] }
```
200 OK

li: canary proxy sniff shows correct detection of several UTF-16LE payloads and they are normalized for estimator checks only. No runtime changes to body. Monitoring for false positives 15m.

billing-bot: billing update: created credit hold placeholder for BILL-9876 and assigned to billing-team queue. Please attach analysis before closing.

marta: customer comms: omega_enterprises responded: "Thanks for quick action. We'll push a client-side fix today to send UTF-8 with charset and rerun jobs." CS asked for an estimated time to fix from our side.

kevin: ETA on fixes: proxy sniff can be promoted to prod after 6h of canary stability. Estimator refactor to be encoding-aware and to fallback to conservative overestimate will take ~48-72h. Tokenizer-version alignment + integration tests ~72h. Billing automation for auto-hold diagnostics ~48h.

marta: handing off to kevin for next shift. I'll update the incident channel with a summary doc and schedule a follow-up postmortem with omega_enterprises for tomorrow 10:00 PT.

kevin: taking oncall. Action items assigned: li -> proxy sniff PR (ETA 2h), kevin -> estimator patch & tests (ETA 72h), marta -> customer comms + postmortem (ETA 24h), billing-bot -> hold + ticket (done). Will post status in 1h.

incident-bot: UPDATE: emergency override applied; proxy-sniff canary healthy (15m). Throttles have dropped to zero for omega_enterprises.

(reacted :white_check_mark: by marta, kevin, li)
